explain.say: The wrinkly outer part of your brain is divided into four main areas on each side, called lobes. Each lobe leads on different jobs, though they all work together.

faq.q: What does the frontal lobe do?
faq.a: The frontal lobe, behind the forehead, helps with planning, decision making, attention, controlling behaviour and speech, and it contains the motor area that starts voluntary movements.
asks: Tell me about the frontal lobe

faq.q: Which part of the brain helps you see?
faq.a: The occipital lobe at the back of the brain is where signals from the eyes are first processed into vision.
asks: Tell me about the occipital lobe

faq.q: What does the temporal lobe do?
faq.a: The temporal lobes, on each side near the ears, process sounds and help with understanding language. Inside them lies the hippocampus, which is important for forming memories.
asks: Tell me about the temporal lobe

faq.a: The cerebellum, at the back underneath the main brain, coordinates movement and balance. It fine-tunes muscle actions so you can walk, write and catch smoothly.

faq.q: Do the two halves of the brain do different things?
faq.a: Mostly they share work, but each half controls the opposite side of the body, and some jobs lean to one side; language, for example, is usually handled mainly on the left.
asks: Why does the left brain control the right side?

facts: The cerebral cortex has four lobes on each side: frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital.
The cerebellum holds more than half of all the brain's nerve cells.

quiz.say: Which lobe first processes what you see?
quiz.show: Which lobe first processes what you see?
quiz.why: Visual signals from the eyes go to the occipital lobe at the back of the brain.
